thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Loses Ground as Bond Yields Climb, Tech Sector Roiled by Apple and Chipmakers

title: Close Update: Wall Street Loses Ground as Bond Yields Climb, Tech Sector Roiled by Apple and Chipmakers
text:
Search Close Update: Wall Street Loses Ground as Bond Yields Climb, Tech Sector Roiled by Apple and Chipmakers April 20, 2018, 04:39:32 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Wall Street was beaten down for a second day on Friday with the major indices lower by more than 1% as rising rates and another steep sell-off in shares of Apple ( AAPL ) eclipsed strong quarterly results from General Electric ( GE ) and Honeywell ( HON ). 
Despite steep losses in the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq, all three still pulled off a positive close for the week with the Dow and S&P 0.4% higher and the Nasdaq up by a slightly better 0.5%. 
The tech sector again took the brunt of recent risk aversion with sluggish iPhone sales dragging down shares of Apple ( AAPL ) and by default, the semiconductor sector which folded on the backlash from the US ban against ZTE Corp. The outcry in China against the US rekindled trade war jitters and sent shares of US chipmakers sharply lower. 
The markets extended early losses later in the day after news circulated that President Trump's campaign was being sued by the Democratic Party for interfering in the 2016 presidential race, and comments from European Central Bank president Mario Draghi conceding defeat in his efforts to boost the EU economy. The turmoil drove the 10-year yield to a two-month high of 2.953%, exacerbating investors' worries about higher borrowing costs. 
On the plus side, corporate earnings were mostly bullish with GE, Honeywell, Ericsson ( ERIC ) and Schlumberger ( SLB ) beating Wall Street's expectations. Skechers (SKX) beat Q1 forecasts, but a downbeat outlook for Q2 caused the stock price to fall by as much as 30% to its lowest level since October (pre-stock split). 
Commodities were under pressure with gold losing another $11 in value, and oil down for most of the day by President Trump's tweet about OPEC behind the "artificially high" prices. Brent crude reversed its losses to close fractionally higher and end the week in the plus column. 
Here's where the markets stood at the close:
